Diagnostic model retrospective | Job 21641

Retrospective analysis

  • Peels. One terminal year of observations was removed at a time, and the model was refitted after each removal. Diagnostic model: 7 retrospective peels (terminal years 2017-2023) from the full-data terminal year 2024.
  • Data. For each peel, all time-dependent inputs were shortened to the same terminal year.
  • Refitting. Each peel used the same model structure and settings as the full-data model and was fitted through the same estimation schedule.
  • Convergence. The maximum gradient component (MGC), the largest absolute objective-function gradient among estimated parameters, was used to assess convergence. The threshold recorded with the retrospective fits was MGC <= 0.001.
  • Annual quantities. Spawning potential and its no-fishing counterpart were summed across regions within each quarter and then averaged by year. Annual depletion is the ratio of these two annual means. Recruitment is the annual sum of numbers entering the first model age. Annual instantaneous fishing mortality is the sum of quarterly population-number-weighted mean F-at-age.
  • Recent management quantities. For each terminal year T, SBrecent and SBF=0 are means over the windows specified by MFCL; their ratio is recent depletion. Diagnostic model: SBrecent T-3 to T (MFCL native four-year default), SBF=0 T-10 to T-1 (MFCL native ten-year default), and recent annual F T-4 to T-1. Recent annual fishing mortality is averaged over the same calendar window for each peel and the full-data fit.
  • First available year. A rolling value is reported only when every calendar year in its window is present and finite; partial early windows are not averaged. Diagnostic model: first SBrecent at T=1955 (1952–1955); first SBF=0 at T=1962 (1952–1961); first recent depletion at T=1962; first recent annual F at T=1956 (1952–1955).
  • Definition check. Window lengths and omitted terminal periods are read from each model rather than assigned to fixed calendar years. The resulting full-data windows follow the WCPFC convention: SBrecent includes T, whereas SBF=0 and recent annual F omit T.
  • Mohn's rho. For each quantity, converged peel estimates were compared with the full-data estimate in the same year. Mohn's rho is their mean relative difference; negative values indicate lower peel estimates and positive values indicate higher peel estimates.
ρX=1|PX|∑p∈PXX^T−p,T−p−X^T−p,TX^T−p,T

Symbols. ρX is Mohn's ρ for quantity X; 𝒫X is the set of converged peels with a finite terminal comparison for X, and |𝒫X| is its size. T is the full-data terminal year and p is the number of terminal years removed. For each estimated quantity in the equation, the first subscript is the year being estimated and the second is the terminal year of the fitted model. The first term in the numerator is therefore the terminal estimate from peel p, and the second is the full-data estimate for that same year.

Source. Mohn (1999) introduced the retrospective statistic. The peel-average form shown here follows Hurtado-Ferro et al. (2015) and the current-practice formulation documented by Legault (2026).

\paragraph{Retrospective analysis.}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Peels.} One terminal year of observations was removed at a time, and the model was refitted after each removal. Diagnostic model: 7 retrospective peels (terminal years 2017-2023) from the full-data terminal year 2024.
\item \textbf{Data.} For each peel, all time-dependent inputs were shortened to the same terminal year.
\item \textbf{Refitting.} Each peel used the same model structure and settings as the full-data model and was fitted through the same estimation schedule.
\item \textbf{Convergence.} The maximum gradient component (MGC), the largest absolute objective-function gradient among estimated parameters, was used to assess convergence. The threshold recorded with the retrospective fits was MGC \textless{}= 0.001.
\item \textbf{Annual quantities.} Spawning potential and its no-fishing counterpart were summed across regions within each quarter and then averaged by year. Annual depletion is the ratio of these two annual means. Recruitment is the annual sum of numbers entering the first model age. Annual instantaneous fishing mortality is the sum of quarterly population-number-weighted mean $F$-at-age.
\item \textbf{Recent management quantities.} For each terminal year T, $\mathrm{SB}_{\mathrm{recent}}$ and $\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$ are means over the windows specified by MFCL; their ratio is recent depletion. Diagnostic model: $\mathrm{SB}_{\mathrm{recent}}$ T-3 to T (MFCL native four-year default), $\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$ T-10 to T-1 (MFCL native ten-year default), and recent annual F T-4 to T-1. Recent annual fishing mortality is averaged over the same calendar window for each peel and the full-data fit.
\item \textbf{First available year.} A rolling value is reported only when every calendar year in its window is present and finite; partial early windows are not averaged. Diagnostic model: first $\mathrm{SB}_{\mathrm{recent}}$ at T=1955 (1952--1955); first $\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$ at T=1962 (1952--1961); first recent depletion at T=1962; first recent annual F at T=1956 (1952--1955).
\item \textbf{Definition check.} Window lengths and omitted terminal periods are read from each model rather than assigned to fixed calendar years. The resulting full-data windows follow the WCPFC convention: $\mathrm{SB}_{\mathrm{recent}}$ includes T, whereas $\mathrm{SB}_{F=0}$ and recent annual F omit T.
\item \textbf{Mohn's rho.} For each quantity, converged peel estimates were compared with the full-data estimate in the same year. Mohn's rho is their mean relative difference; negative values indicate lower peel estimates and positive values indicate higher peel estimates.
\end{itemize}
\[
\rho_X = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}_X|} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_X} \frac{\widehat{X}_{T-p,T-p} - \widehat{X}_{T-p,T}}{\widehat{X}_{T-p,T}}.
\]
Here, $\rho_X$ is Mohn's rho for quantity $X$; $\mathcal{P}_X$ is the set of converged peels with a finite terminal comparison for $X$, and $|\mathcal{P}_X|$ is its size. $T$ is the full-data terminal year and $p$ is the number of terminal years removed. In $\widehat{X}_{a,b}$, $a$ is the year being estimated and $b$ is the terminal year of the fitted model. Thus, $\widehat{X}_{T-p,T-p}$ is the terminal estimate from peel $p$, whereas $\widehat{X}_{T-p,T}$ is the full-data estimate for the same year.
Mohn (1999) introduced the retrospective statistic. The peel-average form shown here follows Hurtado-Ferro et al. (2015) and the current-practice formulation documented by Legault (2026).
\[
\rho_X = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{P}_X|} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_X} \frac{\widehat{X}_{T-p,T-p} - \widehat{X}_{T-p,T}}{\widehat{X}_{T-p,T}}.
\]
Here, $\mathcal{P}_X$ is the set of converged peels with a finite terminal comparison for quantity $X$, $T$ is the full-data terminal year, and $p$ is the number of terminal years removed. In $\widehat{X}_{a,b}$, $a$ is the year being estimated and $b$ is the terminal year of the fitted model.
Mohn (1999) introduced the statistic; the peel-average form follows Hurtado-Ferro et al. (2015) and Legault (2026).

Results

Diagnostic model. For the full-data fit (terminal year 2024), SBrecent was 267.9 thousand t, SBF=0 was 1,547.1 thousand t, and recent depletion (SBrecent/SBF=0) was 0.173. Recent annual fishing mortality was 0.491 year−1. Recent-period Mohn's ρ estimates were: Recent depletion -0.142; Recent spawning potential -0.154; Recent no-fishing spawning potential -0.015; Recent annual instantaneous fishing mortality 0.232.

Diagnostic model. 7 of 7 peel fits converged (100%). Mohn's ρ estimates were: Depletion -0.195 (19.5% lower; 7 peels); Annual F 0.308 (30.8% higher; 7 peels); Recruitment -0.062 (6.2% lower; 7 peels); Spawning potential -0.235 (23.5% lower; 7 peels).

For the biomass-related quantities, Depletion and Spawning potential were outside the -0.15 to 0.20 range proposed for longer-lived simulated species; Spawning potential was outside the -0.22 to 0.30 range proposed for shorter-lived simulated species (Hurtado-Ferro et al., 2015).

Interpretation. The sign of Mohn's rho describes the direction of the peel-to-full-data differences: negative values mean that peel estimates are lower, and positive values mean that they are higher, on average. The Hurtado-Ferro et al. (2015) ranges provide simulation-based context rather than model-specific acceptance criteria because their applicability depends on life history and assessment configuration. Mohn's rho measures retrospective consistency; it does not measure error relative to the unknown true population state and should be considered with other diagnostics (Hurtado-Ferro et al., 2015; Cadrin, 2025).

Appendix. Matched-window annual fishing-mortality diagnostic

For a model fitted through year b, the value evaluated at year t is

F¯t(b)=14∑y=t−4t−1Fy(b)

For peel p, t = T − p, and the peel estimate is compared with the full-data fit over the identical calendar window:

dF,p=F¯T−p(T−p)−F¯T−p(T)F¯T−p(T),ρF=1n∑p=1ndF,p

For the 7 converged peels, ρF = 0.231531.

Annual instantaneous fishing mortality is averaged from T − 4 to T − 1 for each peel and the full-data fit.

\paragraph{Recent fishing-mortality diagnostic.}
For a model fitted through year $b$, the value evaluated at year $t$ is
\[
\overline{F}^{(b)}_{t}=\frac{1}{4}\sum_{y=t-4}^{t-1}F^{(b)}_{y}.
\]
For peel $p$, $t=T-p$ and
\[
d_{F,p}=\frac{\overline{F}^{(T-p)}_{T-p}-\overline{F}^{(T)}_{T-p}}{\overline{F}^{(T)}_{T-p}},\qquad
\rho_F=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{p=1}^{n}d_{F,p}.
\]
For the 7 converged peels, $\rho_F=0.231531$.
Annual instantaneous fishing mortality is averaged over 4 years from $T-4$ to $T-1$.
